title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 26, 2026
headline: WR Jalen Brooks is done for the year, so the WR snaps will be shared by committee (Virgil, Bourne, Fehoko). Jeremiyah Love is due back at practice Wednesday, and Jacoby Brissett remains the starter.
summary: Mike LaFleur opened with the news that WR Jalen Brooks played through an injury from the first quarter and will have surgery today, ending his season. He said the replacement will be by committee, with Reggie Virgil, Kendrick Bourne and Simi Fehoko all in the mix. Jeremiyah Love is expected to practice Wednesday. Walter Nolen is not expected to practice Wednesday, while Max Melton and another player nicknamed 'Dewey' should return. Most of the session was a review of the loss to Denver, where he blamed three explosive defensive plays (a long scramble run, a screen and a deep shot) and offensive detail errors such as poor chip-blocking technique. He took responsibility for the red-zone failures: the team has had ten trips inside the 10 over two games without finishing, and he said he must call better plays. He insisted Brissett is still the starter, with no wrist concerns, and defended not sneaking the ball at the goal line. He said Michael Wilson is running good routes and drawing penalties even without big stats. Bam Knight will keep a role once Love returns. James Conner's injury is not responding as hoped, and he gave only a vague 'potentially' on a return.

topics.detail: Three explosive plays (a long scramble run, a screen pass and a deep shot) drove Denver's scoring. The coach called them correctable: rush-lane discipline, finishing the screen play, and better technique in cloud coverage.
The team ranks last inside the 20 after two bad weeks, but the coach said it isn't a total teardown. He pointed to ten trips inside the 10 over two games and took blame for the play-calling.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Monday, October 26th | Press Conference
headline: Zachariah Branch's role is set to keep growing after a big game, Michael Penix Jr. is trending up in a clean-pocket offense, and no injury news came out of the presser.
summary: Stefanski opened by praising the physical play and the +4 turnover margin in the win over San Francisco, and said the team has to turn the page quickly to a division opponent. He described Michael Penix Jr. as improving with each start, saying he is stacking experience against different coverages, pressures and red-zone looks. Stefanski credited the offensive line for zero sacks and one QB hit, calling a clean pocket the recipe for any quarterback. He called the game an identity game about being physical, pointing to receivers cracking safeties and linemen moving defenders off the ball. He praised Jessie Bates III as a ball-aware safety and a trusted veteran leader, while saying he doesn't focus on scoring statistics. He said Penix takes care of the football but is not a small-ball quarterback and will let it rip down the field when the opportunity is there. On Zachariah Branch, he said Branch played really well, with a big kickoff return, good punt returns and plays in the pass game, and that his role will only continue to grow. No injuries were discussed.

signals.note: Branch is trusted by the coaches and quarterbacks, so he has rising value, especially in PPR or return-yardage formats.
signals.quote: his role will only continue to grow.

signals.claim: Penix will keep attacking downfield and taking shots while protecting the ball in the under-center/pistol/gun offense.
signals.note: He is protected by a clean pocket, takes care of the ball and is not a check-down quarterback, which supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: that's definitely not Mike. And that's not how we coach.

topics.detail: Stefanski said the win was about returning to a physical style of play, which he described as the team's DNA, and he cited receivers' blocking and run-game push up front.
Atlanta is minus three after seven weeks, up from second to last two weeks ago, and the +4 margin against San Francisco was a key to the win.
The offensive line allowed zero sacks and one quarterback hit, which Stefanski framed as the foundation for QB success.
The team has tried competitive periods to open practice and messaging tweaks, but Stefanski said fast starts come down to giving players an understandable plan.

title: Jesse Minter Reflects on Week 7 Loss, Areas for Improvement
headline: Lamar Jackson's availability for Buffalo is unresolved: Minter says he's working hard and 'in a decent spot,' with clarity coming Wednesday. A second, unnamed injury is still TBD. The run game and second-half offense remain unsettled.
summary: Minter opened by calling the loss disappointing, a tale of two halves, and said the Ravens still control their fate over the next ten games, starting with a short week. On Lamar Jackson, he said the QB is working hard, got some work in late last week, and should be in a decent spot, but the team won't know more until Wednesday. He declined to confirm details of the Saturday downgrade (an ankle-swelling report) and said a player who is healthy enough will play. He called the report that the team was shocked by the setback a slight mischaracterization. He said the run game has no single common denominator, pointing to the loss of a key blocking tight end a few weeks ago, younger players being asked to fill roles, and O-line flux. He praised OC Declan Doyle for handling 16 or 17 O-line combinations, Zay Flowers missing a game and Lamar's absence, while pushing back on using Lamar's absence as an excuse. An unnamed player's injury is still TBD, with tests being done Monday and more known Wednesday. He avoided blaming the DBs for trouble covering top receivers, saying it starts with coaching, and he acknowledged the team's second-half struggles and consistency problems. He said the short week (two games in ten days) is a factor in any injury decision.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury; missed the Week 7 game after a Saturday downgrade. Got some work in late last week. Minter says he'll be in a 'decent spot' but status will be clearer Wednesday; the short week is a factor.
Minter mentioned him only as having missed a game earlier in the season; no current status was given.

signals.claim: Lamar's availability for the Buffalo game will be clear by Wednesday; he's expected to be in a decent spot.
signals.note: Lamar's Buffalo status is unresolved, so wait for Wednesday's practice report before setting lineups or making a QB decision.

topics.detail: No single common denominator in the run struggles. Minter cited losing a key blocking tight end a few weeks ago, younger players in bigger roles and O-line flux, and said the staff is searching for schemes and plays the group does well.

The Ravens lead the league in first-half point differential and rank last in the second half. Minter said the numbers show they aren't where they want to be and that all three phases need to improve in halftime and third-quarter adjustments.
Minter praised Doyle, a first-time play caller, for handling 16 or 17 O-line combinations and injuries to Lamar and Flowers, citing strong opening scripts but a need for more consistent adjustments.
Minter wouldn't pin the problems on one cause, saying every play differs by coverage, matchup and technique, and that it starts with coaching putting players in better positions.
Two games in ten days; Minter called the short week a factor in any injury decision.

title: Dave Canales on responding to adversity and preparing for the Packers
headline: Taylor Moton is done for the year after ankle surgery, so Monroe Freeling returns to the OL. Jaelan Phillips, Akayleb Evans, Bobby Brown and Damien Lewis are all day-to-day for Thursday night at Green Bay.
summary: Canales said the team is fully focused on the Packers after a short-week turnaround. Taylor Moton has a fibula fracture below the knee and significant ankle ligament damage, and the ankle surgery ends his season. Canales said Monroe Freeling, who Moton had been mentoring, goes back into the lineup. He watched the full film of the loss to Tampa Bay, praised Tampa's run-game plan, and said the Panthers will study how the Packers might copy it. He declined to share specifics on fixing the run defense beyond saying the fits, leverage and coaching all have to improve, and he called Lathan Ransom's involvement a possibility. Several players are day-to-day: Akayleb Evans (triceps), Bobby Brown (hand), Damien Lewis (knee) and Jaelan Phillips (recurring hamstring, a tight window). On special teams, David Moore fumbled a punt return in a backed-up spot, and Canales said Trevor Etienne has been good catching punts at midfield and the role is under evaluation. Chau Smith-Wade just needs an opportunity. On offense, Canales wants to give Bryce Young quicker answers against pressure, since the Packers will show exotic looks.

title: Dave Canales reflects on Panthers' run defense
headline: Canales says the run defense is being reworked and calls more Lathan Ransom playing time a possibility.
summary: Canales said the Panthers are working on run defense problems but declined to detail the specific adjustments. He said the coaching staff needs to execute better as a group, coach it more collectively, and build a plan so players feel prepared and ready to attack the concepts they will see. He also said the team needs to take away the run game so opponents have to go to other options. When asked about Lathan Ransom, who saw limited snaps until the Bucs game was out of hand, Canales said more playing time is a possibility. He praised Ransom's physicality and said he has been showing up for the team, while noting that Ransom missed a couple of tackles and that the staff has personnel and scheme options to weigh. Canales also said the Bucs had a plan and did not simply hand the ball to Baker Mayfield, who played well and was scrappy. title: Zac Taylor Provides Injury Updates, Reflects on Week 7 Win Over Ravens | PRESS CONFERENCE

Because of the tight end injuries, Jack Endries now moves from the scout team into real playing time and will practice with the starting group catching from Joe Burrow. Taylor praised the defense's red zone and short-yardage play and a clean, penalty-light game on the road. He called Amarius Mims the best tackle he has seen this year and was happy with the offensive line's protection. At halftime Ja'Marr Chase set the tone for the team, and Tee Higgins' big second-half catch sparked the comeback. Taylor shrugged off the stats for Higgins and Chase, saying his comfort with both hasn't changed and production evens out. He also said the team re-signed a tight end, Cam Grandy, as a reliable depth piece, though the corresponding roster move is unannounced. Shemar Stewart was inactive only because the deep D-line forced a tough choice, and Taylor says Stewart is progressing well.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: October 26th, 2026
headline: Quinshon Judkins looked explosive again and the run game improved, Mason Graham is playing through soreness, and the QB room decision (Dillon Gabriel and Clive Davis) is still open before a Week 8 trip to Pittsburgh.
summary: Monken downplayed the five fourth-quarter game-winning drives as a narrative and focused on the team's slow starts, which he said must be fixed (the team has a -45 first-quarter point differential). He said the run game was better because of more consistent game plans, players gaining chemistry and more familiarity with four-down fronts. He praised Quinshon Judkins as powerful and hard to tackle when given room to run, crediting the blocking for the improvement over the last couple of weeks. He credited the auxiliary run game (QB runs, screens, multiple touches) and said Deshaun Watson is part of it. On the early interception, he said the inside receiver got shut off in man coverage and Denzel Boston needed to win the release, but he defended Watson, saying there was nowhere else to go. He spread blame for inconsistency across coaches and players, and called Watson 'under construction' like everyone else. He has not decided on Dillon Gabriel and Clive Davis, calling it part health and part roster management, and joked about carrying four or five QBs. Mason Graham returned but left again; he will be sore for a while and won't be 100% soon. He also confirmed Jared Verse's removal after an offside was partly rotation and partly accountability, but said not to read much into it.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s special teams unit: ‘[The] group has done a real good job’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims Jr. will get more offensive touches, and Jonah Coleman's explosive plays are earning him a bigger role.
summary: Payton praised the Broncos' special teams after a game with big returns, blocked kicks and blocked punts. He called the kicking game the quickest way to improve a team and credited the special teams coach and his group. He said Jonah Coleman played well and that his touches were explosive. He framed more work as something a player earns, and said Coleman has done that. Marvin Mims Jr. went back to kickoff return mainly because of how the opponent was kicking, which led Denver to use a single returner. Payton said the first return put the offense at midfield, and he stressed that Denver needs to get Mims more touches on offense. He was irritated by a question about a reverse call, saying he was answering questions that weren't important and was surprised no one had asked about that call earlier. He also said that the defender in the pressure-rate question has seen his play and confidence trend up, and that he is encouraged by the snap counts and production. He dismissed the idea of rivalry weeks, saying divisional games are simply important.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s win over Arizona: ‘It was one of our more complete games’
headline: Payton says Jonah Coleman looked really good and needs more touches; Bo Nix ran well and Payton firmly backs him as 'our guy' after a complete road win at Arizona.
summary: Payton called the Week 7 road win at Arizona one of the team's more complete games, citing offense, defense and special teams. Denver was aggressive downfield, and Bo Nix's long scramble was framed as a good decision against match coverage that answered the question of whether he can still run. The run game posted a season-high in rushing yards, helped by a plan built around gap schemes and heavier personnel (21 personnel) to keep Arizona out of nickel looks. Payton singled out Jonah Coleman, saying he looked really good and the team has to get him more touches. He said the team's confidence in Nix never changed and that Nix was 'our guy' despite outside questions. On defense he praised the depth that stepped up without Pat (Surtain) and noted Ja'Quan McMillian nearly had a couple of takeaways. Special teams highlights included a blocked punt by Adam Prentice that led to the third touchdown and a Marvin Mims kick return to midfield to open the game. Payton declined to criticize the officials despite a penalty-heavy game, and he took the blame for a poorly conceived reverse call.

title: Campbell on Branch & Reed
headline: Lions are 2-0 in a row, with the D rolling and Branch back. St. Brown and Rakestraw (ankles) are expected back at practice Thursday, and the run game is still inefficient despite Gibbs running hard.

summary: Hafley spoke after his first win as an NFL head coach, a 28-25 division road win over the Jets. He said the win gave a young team confidence and belief, but he stressed that the team has to move on quickly. He is proud of the team's physicality and toughness, citing the goal-line stand, the repeated gap-scheme runs at the end, and the fourth-and-one sneak that sealed the game. He praised Malik Willis for quick decisions, protecting the ball, extending plays with his feet and avoiding sacks, and for moving the clock before halftime. He singled out Greg Dulcich for breaking tackles and making plays, and credited offensive coordinator Bobby (Slowik) for getting him involved. He also praised the non-ball-carriers, including blockers like DJ Herman, Chris Bell, Malik Washington and Will Kacmarek, and the offensive line, especially Jonah Savaiinaea. He called out young defenders Michael Taaffe and Seydou Traore for a miscommunication on the late two-point try. He said the offense uses a mix of gap and outside-zone runs with varied alignments, and that the team will focus on its own growth against a rested Patriots team on Thursday night.

signals.claim: Willis remains the starting quarterback and is developing as a decision-maker who protects the football.
signals.note: The coach singled out Willis' quick decisions, ball security and ability to extend plays, which supports his floor as the starter.
signals.quote: I thought he got the ball out really quick. I thought he played with confidence.

signals.claim: Dulcich will keep being involved in the passing game, including quick throws and plays after the catch.
signals.note: Hafley said the play-caller got him involved and that he made plays in the red area and in zone coverage, which is a good sign for a streaming tight end.
signals.quote: I thought Dulcich played a really good game

signals.note: Kacmarek was praised for his blocking and energy but barely touched the ball, so he has little fantasy value.
signals.quote: he didn't he didn't really touch touch the ball much

signals.note: Herman is used mainly as a blocker and did not touch the ball against the Jets, so he has little fantasy value.
signals.quote: all he does is block and strain and fight

signals.claim: Douglas is back in the receiving corps and could draw more defensive attention.
signals.note: His return could affect the passing game and open up the tight end and run game, but Hafley said little about his usage.

topics.detail: Hafley said the offense mixes gap-scheme and outside-zone runs and changes where the fullback and tight ends line up to create angles and leverage. He said the offensive staff, including Bobby, is figuring out what the team does well.

The team went for it on fourth down to close out the game. Hafley asked the offensive line whether to go for it, and they said yes. He said it reflects the team's identity of toughness and physicality.

Hafley said the defense was strong in the goal-line stand but missed chances to get off the field at 21-7, and Michael Taaffe and Seydou Traore had a miscommunication on the late two-point try. He framed these as learning moments for a young group.
The Dolphins host a rested Patriots team on Thursday night. Hafley said the focus will be on growth and development, starting with game planning that night.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Preparing for Lions in Detroit, Improving Offense & Aaron Jones Injury Day-to-Day
headline: Aaron Jones is day-to-day with Jordan Mason, DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne behind him; Vikings are 6-0 but want more offensive points at Detroit.
summary: O'Connell recapped the Week 7 win over the Colts and said the tape confirmed his first impression. The offense was undone by one-off plays, lost one-on-one blocking matchups up front, and a few missed throws and penalties, which left drives ending in field goals, punts or a turnover on downs. He wants more points and more aggressiveness, including explosive plays off check-downs, while still protecting the football. The only injury update was Aaron Jones being day-to-day. Players who came back from missing time came out clean, so he hopes for a full week of practice. He said he does not see running back depth as an issue because Dallas and Claiborne are in the room, though that could change day to day. He defended Kyler Murray's accuracy and ball security, praised Levi Drake Rodriguez's work at nose tackle and Blake Cashman's play as the defensive green dot, and called Joe Huber's effort strong but said the interior line needs to win more one-on-ones. The Vikings travel to Detroit for a division game against a high-powered offense, and he stressed scoring early as they did in last year's win there.

signals.note: His praise centers on pass protection and special teams, so he is not a clear fantasy-relevant handcuff.
signals.quote: DJ Dallas is doing some really good things in a protection from a protection standpoint

signals.claim: Demond Claiborne is developing and is part of the running back room behind Jordan Mason and Jones.
signals.note: He is a deep-bench stash if Jones misses time.
signals.quote: We still have Damon you know growing every single day.

signals.note: Mason gains value if Jones sits, though the coach did not commit to a workload.

signals.note: The coach backed Murray's accuracy and ball security and wants more points and explosive plays.

signals.note: Interior pass-blocking lapses are affecting Murray's pocket and throws, a mild concern for the offense.
signals.quote: he is playing so hard and competing and battling.

signals.claim: Levi Drake Rodriguez is the starting nose tackle and a key part of the pressure scheme.
signals.note: This is mainly a defensive-lineman note; IDP managers should expect few stats from the role.
signals.quote: I think he's shown the ability to hold up at the point versus double teams

signals.claim: Blake Cashman will keep producing as the defensive green dot with high tackle counts and big plays.
signals.note: He is a strong IDP linebacker with a high tackle floor and play-making upside.
signals.quote: he is now seeing things before they happen.

topics.detail: Stalled drives came from lost one-on-ones up front, short-yardage failures, a holding penalty and late throws. O'Connell wants all 11 players executing, and he wants more aggressiveness and explosives.

The Lions are coming off a big home win and have a high-powered offense in a tough environment. Scoring early helped Minnesota win there last year, and the Vikings are trying to go 3-0 in the NFC North.
Indianapolis sent 7-8 defenders to the line on third-and-7-plus, using zero coverage or spot-drop zone looks. The Vikings had a plan, converted a couple of times and missed on others.
Players returning from missed time came out of the game clean, so a full practice week is expected.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 10/26: "We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team"
headline: Ben Brown may practice this week, Christian Barmore is fine after a scare, and Matt Pryor is earning trust on the offensive line. Vrabel called the run game inconsistent and said the offense needs to improve, including A.J. Brown.
summary: Vrabel said Greg Van Roten and Dell Pettus are eligible to return from IR. He probably won't see Van Roten today but maybe later this week, and a roster decision is pending. He said IR return spots are limited and will be managed by depth and health at each position. The Patriots moved on from punter Bryce Rice, which Vrabel framed as best for both sides, and are sticking with Mitch Wishnowsky, whom he praised. A player they placed on IR is expected to miss at least four games but not the season. Vrabel declined to discuss his $250,000 fine. He defended going for it on fourth down and said they will keep being aggressive. He said Drake Maye's off-script, play-extending ability is valuable. On the run game, he said it has been okay but not consistent, and the offense as a whole, including A.J. Brown and the QB's play fakes, has to do better. He was noncommittal on trade-deadline activity. He praised Matt Pryor's work ethic and play after three weeks, said Ben Brown might practice, and said Christian Barmore was just tired after going down against Chicago.

The Patriots moved on from punter Bryce Rice. Vrabel praised Mitch Wishnowsky's quick get-off, improved plus-50 punts and hangtime.

title: Kellen Moore recaps Week 7 vs. Steelers, bye week 10/26/2026
headline: Saints enter the bye week healthy with no long-term injury concerns, but the run game and slow offensive starts are under full self-scout; Martin Emerson Jr. has earned a starting corner role.
summary: Moore said the team came out of the Paris game against Pittsburgh in good health, with nothing he expects to be a long-term concern, and the bye week gives extra recovery time. The bye week is focused on self-scouting and evaluation, with players coming in for workouts and treatment while coaches hold extended meetings. Moore took ownership of the slow offensive starts as play caller, saying drives have moved the ball and then stalled and that the opening drive has to produce points. He acknowledged the run game was inconsistent, noting a good showing in New York and a poor one against Pittsburgh. He said he felt good about the offseason emphasis on the run game, training camp and joint practices, and that the review will cover schematic and fundamental issues. He said the run game staff structure will not change and described a collaborative process involving the whole offensive staff. Kicking will be evaluated like every other position because of several misses, and he defended the plan of having the kicker travel separately and kick in New Orleans on Friday. He praised Martin Emerson Jr. for his play over the last three weeks, calling him a physical, aggressive corner who earned the start. He used past bye weeks in Philadelphia and Dallas as examples of the team shifting gears and playing well afterward.

injuries.detail: A reporter asked about his throwing hand; Moore said he had not had any conversation about it, so no known concern was confirmed.

signals.claim: Emerson has earned a starting cornerback role and will keep playing meaningful snaps.
signals.note: He is a rising starter in the secondary, which is relevant for IDP leagues.
Moore gave no information on the throwing hand question, so it is worth monitoring, though no issue was confirmed.
signals.quote: I have not had any conversation about that.

topics.detail: The run game was inconsistent, good in New York and poor against Pittsburgh. The bye-week review will cover scheme and fundamentals, and the staff structure for the run game will not change.

Moore said he will focus on how to score on opening drives, since drives have stalled after early success. He pointed out that the Pittsburgh game was a six-possession game, so each possession matters.

The kicker position will be evaluated in the bye-week self-scout after several misses. Moore defended the plan that had the kicker travel Thursday night and kick in New Orleans on Friday before the Paris game.
Players will do workouts and treatment, while the coaches hold evaluation meetings. Moore pointed to past bye weeks in Philadelphia and Dallas that sparked turnarounds.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on heading into the bye week with a win
headline: Giants head into the bye off their best all-around game; Skattebo's big runs and a helmet penalty he disputed stood out, Singletary ('Motor') scored, and the next opponent is the Eagles.
summary: Harbaugh called Sunday's win the team's best-executed, best all-around game on tape. He credited contributions from all three phases and from players who stepped up amid a run of injuries. He said the bye comes at the right time for the nicks, bruises and strains that have built up. Players are in Monday for film review and a workout, and a light 'keep ready' practice and lift follow Tuesday. After that the players are off, and the team returns Monday afternoon to start preparing for the Eagles. Asked why the offense went from second-worst in 20-plus-yard plays (weeks 1-3) to the league lead since, he gave credit to the players: the offensive line, the quarterback, Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely, Malachi Fields and Cam Skattebo. He disagreed with the penalty called on Skattebo for lowering his helmet, saying a back who runs low can't help having his head down, and that the call surprised him. He said the team is not looking at new kickers right now. He also praised players who didn't sulk after being benched or sidelined, naming Motor (Devin Singletary), Skattebo, James/Jameis and JJ as examples. He warned that November will bring physical games.

signals.note: He produced big runs and Harbaugh publicly defended his running style, so his role and workload look secure heading out of the bye.
signals.quote: I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all

signals.note: Singletary scored a touchdown after being out of the lineup, and Harbaugh praised his response, but he gave no word on future snaps.

signals.quote: I'm sure Isaiah has been a big part of that.

Players told coaches the first-time-through game plans had too much in them. Harbaugh acknowledged the team was 'getting over our skis' and said the coaches responded.
Harbaugh expects very physical, tough games in November, and stressed one play at a time and the division and playoff picture as the context.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (10/26) | Week 8
headline: T'Vondre Sweat (knee) is the only injury from Sunday's game, with an update later in the week. Garrett Wilson remains the 'top priority' despite a sideline blowup, and the goal-line carry went to a non-featured back.
summary: Glenn opened by saying injury news will come later in the week, and that T'Vondre Sweat was the only player hurt in the game, with a knee injury. He was disappointed in the loss but said the offense moved the ball and scored better, and that the team played better in the second half after adjustments. A lot of the questioning focused on the end-of-half timeout decision. Glenn said there is a weekly process with the coordinator and kept its details private. He explained he held back timeouts because he feared the opponent would pick up first downs and run out the clock anyway. He admitted the team has to improve in two-minute situations despite repeated practice work. On the goal-line field goal from the one-yard line, he declined to explain who got the carry and said only that the team must score from there. On Garrett Wilson, he said he has spoken with him and that getting him the ball is a priority every game. He said opponents were doubling Wilson, so the offense needs to throw to whoever is open. He called the sideline exchange between Wilson and Geno Smith overblown and said it was about getting the offense going. Jarvis Brownlee was a healthy scratch, and Glenn refused to elaborate, saying it stays in-house. He also said Minkah Fitzpatrick has played well this season despite a missed tackle on a long touchdown, which he shared blame for as play caller.

injuries.detail: Suffered a knee injury in the game and was the only player injured. Glenn will have more information later in the week.

signals.claim: Wilson will remain the top target priority each game, but defenses will keep doubling him, so targets may go to other open receivers.
signals.note: His volume is a stated priority, but heavy double coverage and the coach's emphasis on throwing to open players could cap his targets in some games.
signals.quote: every game Garrett is our top priority to make sure we get the ball.

signals.note: He was a healthy scratch for unexplained reasons, which makes his role uncertain, though he is not a fantasy-relevant player.
signals.quote: I'm going to keep that in-house between, um between me and Jarvis.

signals.note: Glenn publicly backed him despite a missed tackle on a long touchdown, which suggests his role is secure; this matters for IDP only.
signals.quote: I thought Minkah did a really good job

signals.claim: The sideline dispute between Geno Smith and Wilson was minor and the two are on good terms.
signals.note: Glenn downplayed friction between his QB and WR1, so there is no sign of a lasting issue in the passing game.

topics.detail: Glenn defended not using timeouts before halftime, saying the opponent could have kept getting first downs and run out the clock. He said he must do better and that the team practices two-minute drills Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday.
The Jets settled for a field goal after having the ball at the one-yard line. Glenn said the choice of ball carrier did not matter and that the team simply has to score.
He expects outside noise this week and wants the team to tune it out and focus on improving in practice, meetings and walkthroughs.

summary: McCarthy opened by saying he wants to run the ball and was happy with how the touches were distributed in the 16-10 win over New Orleans in Paris. He praised Spencer Anderson's versatility, said the jumbo package was part of the plan from the day he took the job, and said the team wants to keep creating opportunities for him. He framed the four-game stretch as a chance to go 4-0, and the Steelers are 5-2 and tied with Cleveland, which holds the tiebreaker. He credited the offensive and defensive lines, praising Patrick Graham and James Campen, and said the young linemen are contributing. He said the middle linebackers grew thanks to Graham's work and to being cut loose on early pressures, and singled out Payton Wilson's interception as one of the biggest plays of the game. DeShon Elliott was on a play count in his first regular-season game back in nearly a year, and McCarthy said he cleared the first hurdle. He called Aaron Rodgers' mental capacity one of a kind. He said special teams production needs to improve. On Cleveland, he said little has changed on their depth chart and that the short turnaround from the first meeting makes the preparation more current.

title: Todd Bowles on Keeping the Same Energy | Press Conference
headline: Bucs ran for 258 yards in a 30-point win over Carolina. Bucky Irving was praised as the lead back, and Emeka Egbuka and Antoine Winfield Jr. are both questionable for Week 8.
summary: Bowles said the Panthers game went almost exactly to plan: control the clock, run the ball, force turnovers and make plays on special teams. He wants that same intensity every week. The run game carried the day, with 258 rushing yards, and he said Baker Mayfield's light workload (11 pass attempts in his first game back) was not about protecting him. The runs kept working, so they kept calling them. He praised Bucky Irving's mental toughness, work ethic and ability to cut at full speed, and said all three running backs got downhill well. Benjamin Chukwuma made his first start of the year on the offensive line and Bowles said he has a huge future as a full-time starter. Egbuka (concussion and foot) and Winfield are among three players listed as questionable, and he'll know more after Wednesday and Thursday practices. He reported no new injuries from the game. He also explained choosing to receive the opening kickoff: he wanted to see the offensive line and establish the run early. The defense got a blocked extra point and a two-point return, and the sacks finally arrived after weeks of pressure.

injuries.detail: Dealing with both a concussion and a foot injury, which Bowles said were about equally responsible for him missing Sunday. Bowles will have a better answer after Wednesday and Thursday practices.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh backs Cam Ward as a work in progress after a loss, keeps Michael Carter ahead of Nick Singleton on third downs, and Alontae Taylor sat out all defensive snaps in favor of Josh Williams.
summary: Saleh opened by saying there were no new injury updates and that evaluations are ongoing. He called the defensive performance against Cleveland disappointing, citing poor tackling, too many explosive plays, run defense that was not up to standard, and a pass rush that lacked impact. He defended Cam Ward, saying he played good but not exceptional winning football and that the loss shouldn't be pinned on him. He admitted Ward's footwork lapses are unacceptable, but said old habits are hard to break under pressure and need reps. He said teammates must also help through protection, route running and play calling. On the backfield, he said Michael Carter has more three-down value than Nick Singleton because of pass protection and third-down understanding, though Singleton is still growing. Alontae Taylor was active but did not play, as the staff wanted to give Josh Williams more run after a good game against Indianapolis, and they are working Taylor into the complicated nickel role. Saleh described Kevin Winston's first game back as not alarming, though he could have been better, and said the team has a finishing problem, going 1-4 in one-score games.

summary: Quinn opened with injury updates: Treylon Burks is working back into practice, Javon Kinlaw's knee is progressing slower than hoped, and Marcus Mariota and Charles Omenihu return to practice. He called the bye a much-needed reset, with separate self-scouts for each phase, and wants more consistent fight and execution across all four quarters. He explained that Steve Wilks was added to help with defensive game planning early in the week, a move discussed since training camp. On Jayden Daniels, he agreed there is some merit to the critique about aggressiveness on tight-window throws in certain games, but praised his accuracy and deep-ball placement. With McLaurin out, Quinn said Diggs' workload shouldn't change much, but Antonio Williams should climb to higher target volume. He said the offensive line fixes are about strategy more than personnel, focused on the run game, finishing blocks, and downfield blocking. Croskey-Merritt is still working through a groin injury and the team will be cautious, so the backfield for this week leans on other backs, including McNichols and Rachaad White.
